name: Sapphire Foods India Ltd
title: Sapphire Foods India Ltd - 543397 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Restaurant operator with no capacity discipline signal: KFC SSSG 14% (near double-digit ex-Navratri) driven by value, marketing up, margins guided to pressure from Q3; Pizza Hut expansion frozen to CY26.

summary.headline: Sapphire Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% to INR885 crore and adjusted EBITDA 39% to INR62.4 crore, driven by value-led transaction growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 20% YoY to INR885 crore, the best revenue growth since the COVID period per management, with 15 KFC and 1 Pizza Hut Sri Lanka openings taking the restaurant count to 1,086. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA rose 39% to INR62.4 crore (7.1% margin, up 100 bps), while post-Ind AS PBT was minus INR60 lakh. KFC SSSG of 14% (close to double digit after adjusting for Navratri timing) and Pizza Hut SSSG of 5% were driven by entry-value offers (INR99/INR149 meals, BOGO) and higher marketing spend. Management flagged cost inflation (minimum wages, energy, poultry, cheese) peaking in Q3 FY27 and chose growth over pricing.

financial_highlights.change: up 20 bps YoY; restaurant EBITDA up 21% YoY
up from INR31.9 crore in Q1 FY27
15 KFC and 1 Pizza Hut (Sri Lanka) added in quarter

segments.name: KFC India
segments.commentary: SSSG 14% (close to double digit after Navratri shift), overall revenue growth 26%, gross margin 67.7% (up 50 bps), restaurant EBITDA 14.5% (up 70 bps). Dine-in and takeaway mix rose to 57%; fourth consecutive quarter of positive SSSG; 80% of restaurants have digital kiosks.

segments.name: Pizza Hut India
segments.commentary: SSSG 5% (highest in 7 quarters), overall revenue growth 7%, gross margin 76.3% (up 190 bps, helped by 2-3% price increase taken around June 2026), restaurant EBITDA loss of 2.8%. Delivery mix 52%; second consecutive quarter of positive SSSG with double-digit SSTG.

segments.name: Sri Lanka
segments.commentary: SSSG 5% and revenue growth 9% in LKR terms; gross margin largely stable; restaurant EBITDA 12.5%, hit by energy and wage inflation. Dine-in and takeaway 61%, delivery 39%; one store opened in Dehiwala.

guidance_outlook: KFC store additions for FY27 remain at 60-80 stores; Pizza Hut expansion expected to be neutral in calendar 2026 with no new stores.
Management expects cost inflation to peak in Q3 FY27; input cost increases expected to be slightly higher in Q3 from current levels on both brands.
Marketing spend for FY27 to rise 50-100 bps of sales for KFC and 100-150 bps for Pizza Hut versus FY26.
Management said combined Q2 and Q3 FY27 KFC SSSG should be high single digit, with festive shift adding roughly 4-5%; Pizza Hut does not benefit from the shift.
Management will be cautious on pricing and prioritise growth; some margin pressure expected in coming quarters but cost recovery is expected once growth is sustained.
No additional borrowings expected in the near future.
capex_capacity: KFC: 15 restaurants added in Q2 FY27; 60-80 store additions planned for FY27.
Store mix: about 60% to two-thirds of KFC openings in metros (cities above 1 million population); 70-80% of openings in cities where the company already operates.
Pizza Hut: no store openings in calendar 2025; none planned in calendar 2026, pending CCI approval for the Devyani-Sapphire alignment.
Borrowings of about INR30-36 crore on balance sheet described as a multipurpose long-term loan for expansion; finance cost is mainly Ind AS 116 lease cost.
demand_pricing: KFC SSSG of 14% was over 50% transaction-driven, with the balance from average price per customer (APC); repeat rate of 60-70% among first-time customers who tried INR99 or INR149 offers, with ticket size rising on return visits.
Price increases of 2-3% taken in KFC in April or May 2026 and in Pizza Hut in June 2026; management said it will be very careful with further pricing.
Input inflation: minimum wages up 26% in Karnataka, energy (gas and electricity) cost increases, poultry inflation affecting KFC; cheese covered through at least Q2 FY27.
Pizza Hut SSSG of 5% treated as is without a veg/non-veg adjustment; veg-to-non-veg mix roughly 70:30.
Sri Lanka SSSG held up at 5% despite inflation tied to the Middle East conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 4-5% festive-shift benefit imply a mid-single-digit trend for the December quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified that Q2 plus Q3 FY27 combined should come in at high single-digit SSSG; Pizza Hut gets no festive shift benefit.

qa_highlights.question: How much of KFC SSSG is transaction-led versus ticket-led, and do INR99/BOGO recruits repeat?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 50% of SSSG is transaction-driven, with the rest APC; repeat rate of 60-70% among first-time value customers, and ticket size rises on repeat visits.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company moderate promotional intensity given margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is less concerned about gross margin; it is willing to give up a few bps of gross margin if it lifts SSSG via transactions, with restaurant EBITDA already improving.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change to the 60-80 KFC store guidance and what is the Pizza Hut expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: KFC guidance unchanged at 60-80 stores; no Pizza Hut openings in 2026, and brand alignment with Devyani awaits CCI approval, after which a couple of quarters are needed before the brand fires.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise and why is there new borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost mostly reflects Ind AS 116 lease accounting tied to store additions; the INR30 crore borrowing is a small multipurpose long-term loan and no further borrowing is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Pizza Hut gross margin sustainability and value-offer mix impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 gain was from the price increase and reduced online discounting; the value-offer mix was not materially different quarter on quarter, and management will accept a few bps of margin loss for throughput.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of KFC store openings by city tier and by new versus existing cities?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% to two-thirds of openings in metros with over 1 million population; 70-80% in cities where the company already operates.

qa_highlights.question: Do festive shifts change KFC gross margin, and how does channel profitability compare?
qa_highlights.answer: No material gross margin change during the festive period and no special promotions; dine-in and takeaway have slightly lower gross margin than delivery but higher restaurant-level flow-through because there are no delivery commissions or delivery costs.

qa_highlights.question: What marketing spend increase is planned for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: KFC marketing up 50-100 bps and Pizza Hut up 100-150 bps versus FY26.

risks_watch: Cost inflation (wages, energy, poultry, cheese) is expected to peak in Q3 FY27 and may compress margins if SSSG growth slows.
Pizza Hut restaurant EBITDA is negative at -2.8%; turnaround depends on CCI approval and alignment with Devyani.
Pricing restraint: management is cautious on further price increases, so cost recovery may be delayed.
Whether KFC SSSG holds once the Navratri shift reverses and value-offer-driven recruitment normalises.
Sri Lanka restaurant EBITDA margin of 12.5% is under pressure from energy and wage inflation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and transaction growth, with repeated emphasis on value offers and higher marketing spend. Cautious and candid on cost inflation and the margin outlook, saying Q3 FY27 will see inflation peak and pricing will be handled carefully. Evasive on the exact inflation percentage and on Pizza Hut's timeline for store-level profitability.
key_quotes: We delivered the best quarter of revenue growth, 20% and adjusted EBITDA growth 39% since the COVID period, that is since the last 16 quarters.

Most companies will be cautious and reduce marketing spends. We are going against the tide and actually increasing marketing spend because we believe we've got strong everyday value that entices the consumers to come to our stores.
So more than 50% of the SSSG would be transaction driven and the balance would be the APC driven.
We must be very careful, Devanshu.

adds.what: KFC restaurants: 60-80 store additions planned for FY27 (15 added in Q2 FY27)
Pizza Hut: no new store openings planned in calendar 2026

growth.why: Management held KFC FY27 store additions at 60-80 (15 opened in Q2 so far) and guided high single-digit combined Q2-Q3 KFC SSSG with a festive shift adding 4-5%, backed by transaction-led demand and 15 openings, while Pizza Hut has no new stores in CY26 and cost inflation peaks in Q3 FY27.
